3.  Pledge of Revenue Agreement with CalRecycle for Postclosure Maintenance of Pebbly
  Beach Landfill
  California Code of Regulations requires operators of solid waste landfills to demonstrate
  the availability of financial resources to conduct closure, postclosure maintenance, and
  corrective action activities . The City has $3 .79 million in restricted trust funds committed
  to postclosure maintenance as of June 30 , 2025 . The State regulations allow another
  mechanism to demonstrate the availability of financial resources: a Pledge of Revenue .
  Recommended Action
  Adopt a resolution approving a Pledge of Revenue Agreement with the California
  Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery for postclosure maintenance fo r the
  Pebbly Beach Landfill , Facility No. 19-AA-0061 .

4.  Harbor Vehicle Replacement
  The Harbor Department requires a dependable and versatile road vehicle to carry out
  Harbor activities including responding to emergency calls on land , support of patrol
  operations and storm-duty. The current Harbor Patrol vehicle is a 19-year-old Ford
  Explorer that currently requires major repairs including front-end work, windshield
  replacement, engine repairs and major rust damage repair.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize City Manager, or his designee, to purchase a used 2019-2024 Ford Ranger to
  replace the current Harbor Patrol vehicle , a 2006 Ford Explorer, for an amount not-to-
  exceed sum of $42 ,000 .

GENERAL BUSINESS

5.  Approval of Encroachment Permit for Private Improvements within the Public Right-of-
  Way at 358 Claressa Ave.
  An application for an Encroachment Permit was submitted for the property located at 358
  Claressa Ave. The application was received on July 28 , 2025 , and proposes two
  encroachments into the public right-of-way.
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
SEPTEMBER 16, 2025
PAGE3

  Recommended Action
  1. Approve encroachment permit at 358 Claressa Ave for the construction of a new
  staircase within the public alley (between Claressa and Catalina Avenues) providing a
  secondary access to the second-floor unit, a new balcony on the second-floor, and a patio
  at grade on the first-floor dwelling unit both encroaching up to 22-inches into the Claressa
  Avenue right-of-way . 2. Authorize City Manager or his designee to approve to finalize and
  execute  the  encroachment  permit,  associated  recordable  maintenance
  covenant/easement, and to negotiate with the property owners the amounts of the
  required bond and liability insurance.

6.  First Reading of an Ordinance Amending Chapter 9-5 , Article 5 (UM - Low and Moderate
  Income Housing) and Article 6 (Accessory Dwelling Units) of Title 9 of the Avalon
  Municipal Code, implementing housing programs 14 and 15 as set forth in the 6th Cycle
  General Plan Housing Element and Adoption of Exemption Findings Under the Californ ia
  Environmental Quality Act
  In September 2022 , the City Council adopted the 2021-2029/6th Cycle General Plan
  Housing Element. The Housing Element is a state-mandated section of the General Plan
  which identifies the housing needs , opportunities , and constraints in the City of Avalon .
  The Housing Plan section of the Housing Element further sets forth the City's goals ,
  policies and programs to address Avalon 's identified housing needs. Some programs
  require one-time code amendments, while others have ongoing review schedules that
  require monitoring legislative actions and regular updates to the Avalon Municipal Code
  (AMC).
  Recommended Action
  Introduce and waive all readings of an ordinance of the City of Avalon amending Chapter
  9-5 , Article 5 (UM - Low and Moderate Income Housing) and Article 6 (Accessory
  Dwelling Units) of Title 9 of the Avalon Municipal Code, implementing housing programs
  14 and 15 as set forth in the 6th Cycle General Plan Housing Element and adoption of
  exemption findings under the California Environmental Quality Act.

7.  Motorola Portable APX8000 Series Radio Procurement
  The City of Avalon Fire Department needs LA RICS compatible radios . Utilizing
  cooperative procurement methods as outlined in Avalon Municipal Code Section 3-
  4.111 (d) the City of Avalon requested quotes from Motorola Solutions for new radios .
  Recommended Action
  1. Make the affirmative finding to exempt this procurement from competitive bidding
  requirements due to utilization of cooperative bidding procedures as outlined in Avalon
  Municipal Code Section 3-4 .111 (d) . 2. Authorize the City Manager, and/or his designee,
  to execute a contract with Motorola Solutions to purchase four (4) new portable Motorola
  APX 8000 Radios for a not-to-exceed sum of $65,000 as budgeted in the City's Fiscal
  Year 2025-26 Capital Improvement Plan , Project #254501 , Account #10245-6547 .
 CITY COUNCIL AGENDA
SEPTEMBER 16, 2025
PAGE4

8.  Maintenance Services Agreement with Perry Plumbing & Pipelining to Epoxy Lining
  Repairs of Sewer Mains
  The City maintains an extensive sewer collection system , portions of which are
  constructed of verified clay pipe (VCP) . Over time , these lines are prone to cracking and
  root intrusion , which cause blockages, backups, and costly emergency repairs . To extend
  the service life of existing public works infrastructure, staff have identified two segments
  of sewer main requiring epoxy lining rehabilitation .
  Recommended Action
  Per the City's procurement policy, authorize the City Manager, or his designee, to execute
  an agreement with Perry Plumbing & Pipelining to provide maintenance services for the
  installation of epoxy lining of two verified clay sewer mains in the amount not-to-exceed
  $32 ,036.

ADJOURN

SUBJECT:  Pledge of Revenue Agreement with CalRecycle for
  Postclosure Maintenance of Pebbly Beach Landfill

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Adopt a resolution approving a Pledge of Revenue
Agreement with the California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery for
postclosure maintenance for the Pebbly Beach Landfill , Facility No. 19-AA-0061 .

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon 's Pebbly Beach Landfill has less than two years
left of life. The City, in conjunction with CR&R, is working to optimize the life of the landfill
through a capital infrastructure project currently under review of Los Angeles County
Regional Planning . If approved by Los Angeles County, the construction of an eighteen
foot mechanically stabilized earth wall will extend the life of the landfill for 25-27 years
given current use.

California Code of Regulations Title 27, Division 2, Subdivision 1, Chapter 6 (the
"Regulations") requires operators of solid waste landfills to demonstrate the availability of
financial resources to conduct closure , postclosure maintenance , and corrective action
activities . The minimum period to fund a landfill after closure is 30 years , or until no longer
deemed a threat by regulatory agencies .

The City currently uses the restricted enterprise fund mechanism in accordance with
§22241 of the regulations for financial obligations for closure , postclosure maintenance ,
and corrective action. The City currently has $3 .79 million in restricted trust funds
committed to postclosure maintenance as of June 30 , 2025 .

The State regulations allow another mechanism to demonstrate the availability of financial
resources : a Pledge of Revenue. A Pledge of Revenue is an agreement between the City
of Avalon and the California Department of Resources Recycling and Recovery
(CalRecycle) wherein the City commits to budgeting the costs of postclosure maintenance
each year instead of funding the full 30 years with restricted cash reserves .

With the proposed added capacity of the Pebbly Beach Life Optimization Project, the
Pebbly Beach Landfill is not expected to reach capacity until fiscal year 2051/2052. The
City has already budgeted $500,000 in the solid waste fund for planning , environmental
review, and design . The City currently estimates construction costs to be at three million .
 By approving the resolution and changing the funding mechanism of the trust fund method
to the pledge of revenue method will allow for these funds to be used for the capital project
toward Phase 1 of wall construction. This will also provide additional time for the City to
accumulate revenues for Phase 2 and Phase 3 of construction .

The pledge of revenue mechanism requires the City to enter into an agreement with
CalRecycle to memorialize the City's financial commitment for postclosure maintenance.
City staff drafted the agreement with concurrence from the City Attorney's Office and
CalRecycle staff. If the pledge is approved by City Council and Calrecycle , the City's
pledge amount postclosure shall be equal to $79 ,274 (in 2025 dollars) per year for the
state mandated period of postclosure maintenance.

FISCAL IMPACTS: By changing the funding mechanism from the restricted enterprise
trust fund to a pledge of revenue will allow funds that would otherwise be used to fund
post-closure costs to become available in the Solid Waste Fund . These funds will be used
for the Pebbly Beach Landfill Life Site Optimization Project and improve solvency with the
Solid Waste Fund .

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Improved Business Efficiency

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: None.

FOLLOW UP ACTION : Execute the resolution and agreement documents with
CalRecycle . Conduct appropriate fund transfers to the Solid Waste Fund .

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: The item was properly listed on the
posted agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S) : Introduce and waive all readings of an ordinance of the City of
Avalon amending Chapter 9-5 , Article 5 (UM - Low and Moderate Income Housing) and Article
6 (Accessory Dwelling Units) of Title 9 of the Avalon Municipal Code , implementing housing
programs 14 and 15 as set forth in the 6th Cycle General Plan Housing Element and adoption of
exemption findings under the California Environmental Quality Act.

BACKGROUND: On September 20 , 2022 , the City Council adopted the 2021-2029/6th Cycle
General Plan Housing Element. The Housing Element is a state-mandated section of the
General Plan which identifies the housing needs , opportunities, and constraints in the City of
Avalon . The Housing Plan section of the Housing Element further sets forth the City's goals ,
policies and programs to address Avalon 's identified housing needs , including production of 27
new housing units as allocated by the Southern California Association of Governments (SCAG)
Regional Housing Needs Assessment (RHNA) for the 6th review cycle .

The Housing Plan contains 26 programs adopted to implement the goals and policies of the
Housing Element. Some programs require one-time code amendments, while others have
ongoing review schedules that require monitoring legislative actions and regular updates to the
Avalon Municipal Code (AMC). Over the next several months , the Planning and Building
Department will bring forth a series of code amendments for consideration to implement all of
the housing programs to ensure the City continues to be compliant with State law. The
amendments proposed at this time are intended to address the requirements of Program #14
(Accessory Dwelling Units) and Program #15 (Adequate Sites for Lower Income Households on
Nonvacant and Vacant Sites Previously Identified) .

PROGRAM #14-ACCESSORY DWELLING UNITS: Accessory dwelling units (ADUs) and
junior accessory dwelling units (JADUs) help meet the City's housing needs for all income
levels and also provide a housing resource for seniors and low- and moderate-income
households throughout the entire community. In accordance with State law, accessory units
(also known as second units or granny flats) are allowed by right in all residential zones
within the city. Chapter 9-5 , Article 6 , Accessory Dwelling Units, provides specific
development standards and processing requirements for ADUs .

Program #14 requires that the City continue to amend the ordinance based on future
changes to State law and work with the California Department of Housing and Community
 Development (HCD) to ensure continued compliance with State law. The City will also
continue to monitor the extent of ADU production to ensure that the ordinance modifications
are successful and that the Housing Element goals can be met.

SB 1211 and AB 2553 , adopted in 2024 and effective as of January 1, 2025 , are the most
recent legislative acts that include multiple updates to State ADU law which clarify the
development requirements for AD Us. Below is a summary of the amendments proposed to
comply with current State law requirements :

  •  Update Government Code and Health and Safety Code legal references throughout.
  •  Add definition for "livable space". (Section 9-5.603)
  •  Clarify the number of detached ADUs permitted on a lot with proposed multi-family
  development. (Section 9-5 .604.a.4)
  •  Clarify that JADUs are only permitted on lots zoned for single-family residences .
  (Section 9-5.605.a .3)
  •  Clarify the method of measuring the height of an ADU . (Section 9-5.605 .b.5)
  •  Remove owner-occupancy requirement for ADUs constructed after January 1, 2025.
  (Section 9-5 .605 .g.1 and 2)
  •  Clarify that uncovered parking spaces are included in the types of off-street parking
  that do not need to be replaced when an ADU is constructed (Section 9-5.606.g.3)
  •  Add clarification of the number of allowed stories for an ADU . (Section 9-6.606.j)

In addition , Staff has reviewed the objective architectural design standards for ADUs to
identify opportunities to clarify requirements and reduce impediments for ADU development.
The following amendments are proposed to update the design standards for ADUs:

  •  Clarify the architectural requirements for window and door placement and privacy
  screening . (Section 9-5.606 .h.5)
  •  Add architectural requirement that roof slope must match that of the dominant roof
  slope of the primary dwelling on a lot. (Section 9-5.606 .h.7)
  •  Revise the requirements for site landscaping to require compliance with the objective
  standards of the underlying zone. (Section 9-5 .606 .i)

Complete amendment language is included in the draft ordinance (Attachment 1) and strike-
through amendment text (Attachment 2) . It is the opinion of staff that the proposed amendments
comply with existing State law concerning ADUs and fully implements Program #14 of the 6th
Cycle Housing Element.

PROGRAM #15 - ADEQUATE SITES FOR LOWER INCOME HOUSEHOLDS ON
NONVACANT AND VACANT SITES PREVIOUSLY IDENTIFIED: As part of the Housing
Element development process, local governments are required to prepare an inventory of land
suitable for residential development, including vacant sites and sites having the potential for
redevelopment. During the preparation of the 6th Cycle Housing Element, one site on Tremont
Street (APN 7480-002-072) was identified as a housing opportunity site with potential to
accommodate the number of units required to meet the city's RHNA unit allocation . A map
showing the location of the subject parcel is provided as Attachment 3.

Program #15 of the Housing Element is intended to provide streamlined review of high-density
housing projects on the Tremont Street property which include affordable housing units. Program
#15 states:
   "The City of Avalon will rezone to allow developments by right pursuant to Government
  Code section 65583.2(i) when 20 percent or more of the units are affordable to lower
  income households on sites identified in Appendix A to accommodate the lower income
  RHNA that was previously identified in past housing elements. Specifically, the City will
  rezone the 1.52-acre nonvacant site located at Tremont Street (APN 7480-002-072)
  previously identified in the 5th cycle housing element. "

The Tremont Street property is currently zoned Low and Moderate Income Housing (LIM) and
is designated High Density Residential - Community Housing in the General Plan Land Use
Element. Pursuant to AMC Section 9-5.502 , low and moderate income housing as defined in
AMC Chapter 9-11 is permitted by right in the LIM zone, and the maximum permitted density is
40 dwelling units per acre. Therefore , the property is already appropriately zoned for compliance
with Program 15.

To further clarify implementation of Program #15 , Staff proposed that a new AMC Section 9-
5.505 be added to Chapter 9-5, Article 5 of Title 9 (LIM - Low and Moderate Income Housing),
which states that residential development on the Tremont Street property shall be considered a
by-right use, and may be processed without discretionary review, when at least 20 percent or
more of units are reserved for affordable to low and very low income households and the project
has a density of at least 30 dwelling units per acre. Complete amendment language is included
in the draft ordinance (Attachment 1) and strike-through amendment text (Attachment 2) .

It is the opinion of staff that the proposed amendments LIM zone fully implement Program #15
of the Housing Element.The Tremont Street property is owned by the Santa Catalina Island
Company and is already partially developed with residential units. In compliance Program #15 ,
if the City receives an application for a housing development project during this cycle, the City
will notify HCD and process the application consistent with State law.

PLANNING COMMISSION RECOMMENDATIONS: On September 3, 2025 , the Planning
Commission held a duly noticed public hearing at which time written and oral evidence was
considered regarding the proposed amendments is included as Attachment 4 of this report. The
Planning Commission adopted Planning Commission Resolution No. 25-49, which recommends
adoption of the proposed ordinance by the City Council , with the following additional
recommendations regarding off-street parking requirements for ADUs and JADUs:

  •  Access to the City of Avalon Seaside Transit (COAST) transit system shall be considered
  as public transit for the purpose of applying exemption criteria from providing off-street
  parking spaces for ADUs and JADUs.

AMC Section 9-5.606.g provides several possible exemptions from providing off-street parking
for ADUs and JADUs, as provided by State law. Specifically, AMC Section 9-5 .606 .g.a states
that no off-street parking space is required when the ADU is located within one-half mile walking
distance of public transit, as defined by AMC Section 9-5.603 .

The definition of "public transit" in AMC Section 9-5.603 is based on the Government Code
definition for public transit as set forth in Gov Code Section 66313(m) , which defines public
transit as "a location , including , but not limited to , a bus stop or train station, where the public
may access buses, trains , subways , and other forms of transportation that charge set fares , run
on fixed routes , and are available to the public". COAST does not meet the State definition of
public transit, as it operates as an on-demand service and does not run on a fixed route.
 The Planning Commission recommends that due to the unique nature of COAST as an on-
demand transit system , that the applicable AMC section be amended to incorporate COAST as
a qualifier for the ADU parking exemption criteria .

It is the opinion of staff that expanding the definition of "public transit" to include COAST on-
demand transit system does not conflict with State law, as the City is expanding opportunities to
eliminate off-street parking requirements . This is consistent with the intent of applicable State
law for ADU parking regulations that intend to decrease barriers to the construction of ADUs.
Therefore, staff has updated the definition of "public transit" in AMC Section 9-5 .603, and the
amended language is reflected in the draft ordinance and strike-through amendment text. As
proposed , nearly all residential properties within the city will qualify for a parking exemption as
long as they have access to the public right-of-way.

  •  Should a property owner wish to acquire an autoette vehicle permit for the ADU/JADU ,
  then the property would be required to provide off-street parking to be eligible for an
  autoette vehicle permit.

At this time, ADUs and JADUs are not eligible for autoette permits pursuant to AMC Section 4.4-
1703.g.9. However, the ADU regulations currently require that an off-street parking space be
provided regardless , unless one of the parking space exemption criteria are met. To bring the
parking space requirements and vehicle permit qualifications into alignment, Planning
Commission recommended that if the residents of an ADU wished to have a vehicle permit, then
appropriate off-street parking should be required to reduce on-street parking congestion.
Otherwise, off-street parking should not be required in order to lessen the development
constraints for new ADUs.

At the March 4, 2025 , regular meeting , the City Council provided direction to staff to consider
revisions to the vehicle code to allow ADUs to be granted autoette permits , so long as
appropriate off-street parking is provided for the vehicle. Therefore , the Planning Commission's
recommendation is in line with previous direction provided by the City Council.

Staff has added the recommended off-street parking exemption language as AMC Section 9-
5.606.g .2.g in both the draft ordinance and strike-through amendment text. Ad proposed , ADUs
shall be exempt from providing off-street parking unless the resident or owner maintains a valid
autoette permit for the unit. However, a separate text amendment to AMC Section 4.4-1703 .g.9
is required before any ADU or JADU resident may apply for an autoette permit, which City
Council may undertake as a separate action .

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION : The Avalon Municipal
Code will not be amended , and the City will be out of compliance with the mandated
implementation programs set forth in the 6th Cycle General Plan Housing Element.

Section 4. CEQA Exemptions.
The ordinance is exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental Quality Act
(CEQA) per State CEQA Guidelines Sections 15183(a) and 15601 (b)(3) because it has
no potential to have a significant effect on the environment and is not subject to CEQA.

The General Plan is a long-term policy guide for the development of the City but does not
propose specific development that can be analyzed at a project-specific level. Therefore ,
the General Plan EIR is a Program EIR (State Clearinghouse No. 2011091042) . A
Program EIR provides a more general analysis of the General Plan that focuses on the
overall effects of implementation of the General Plan . The 6th Cycle General Plan Housing
Element was adopted in September 2022 . An addendum to the Program EIR was
prepared which concluded that the Housing Element updates do not result in any new or
greater environmental impacts than were previously analyzed , disclosed, and mitigated .

Pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21083 .3 and CEQA Guideline 15183(a), a
project that is consistent with the development densities established in a General Plan for
which an EIR was certified is not required to undergo additional environmental review
"except as might be necessary to examine whether there are project-specific significant
effects which are peculiar to the project or its site ." As noted above , an EIR was certified
for the General Plan. The amendments contained in the ordinance do not authorize
construction and make minor changes to existing standards and land use limitations that
apply to existing uses permitted in residential zones in the City and allow uses that are
consistent with the residential uses currently permitted in such zones.

In addition , Guideline 15061 (b)(3) states that a project is exempt from CEQA if the activity
covered by the common sense exemption that CEQA only applies to projects which have
 the potential for causing a significant effect on the environment. The amendments provide
standards for the approval of allowed growth within the parameters of existing General
Plan and municipal code regulations . It does not authorize any changes to land use
limitations or approve any new development project. Therefore, there is no reasonable
possibility that the activity in question may have a significant effect on the environment.

Further, California Public Resources Code section 21080 .17 provides that the California
Environmental Quality Act ("CEQA") does not apply to the adoption of an ordinance by a
city or county implementing the provisions of Section 65852 .1 or Section 65852 .2 of the
Government Code , which is California's ADU law and which also regulates JADUs, as
defined by section 66313. Therefore, the component of the ordinance which implements
state ADU law is statutorily exempt from CEQA.

Therefore, it can be seen with certainty that the ordinance has no potential to cause a
significant effect on the environment, and the amendments themselves are categorically
exempt from further review under CEQA pursuant to Sections 15183(a) and 15061 (b)(3)
of the California Code of Regulations .

§ 9-5.601 Purpose.
The purpose of this section is to allow and regulate accessory dwelling units (ADUs) and
junior accessory dwelling units (JADUs) in compliance with Chapter 13 of Division 1 of
Title 7 of the California Government Code.

§ 9-5.602 Effect of Conforming.
An ADU or JADU that conforms to the standards in this section will not be :
(a) Deemed to be inconsistent with the City's general plan and zoning designation for
the lot on which the ADU or JADU is located.
(b) Deemed to exceed the allowable density for the lot on which the ADU or JADU is
located .
(c) Considered in the application of any local ordinance , policy, or program to limit
residential growth.
(d) Required to correct a nonconforming zoning condition , as defined in subsection 9-
5.603 below. This does not prevent the City from enforcing compliance with applicable
building standards in accordance with Health and Safety Code section 17980.12.

§ 9-5 .603 Definitions.
As used in this section , terms are defined as follows :
ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or ADU
  Means an attached or a detached residential dwelling unit that provides complete
  independent living facilities for one or more persons and is located on a lot with a
  proposed or existing primary residence . An accessory dwelling unit also includes
  the following:
  (a) An efficiency unit, as defined by section 17958.1 of the California Health and
  Safety Code ; and
  (b) A manufactured home , as defined by section 18007 of the California Health
  and Safety Code.
ACCESSORY STRUCTURE
  Means a structure that is accessory and incidental to a dwelling located on the
  same lot.
COMPLETE INDEPENDENT LIVING FACILITIES
   Means permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating , cooking , and sanitation
  on the same parcel as the single-family or multifamily dwelling is or will be
  situated .
EFFICIENCY KITCHEN
  Means a kitchen that includes all of the following:
  (a) A cooking facility with appliances .
  (b) A food preparation counter and storage cabinets that are of a reasonable size
  in relation to the size of the JADU .
JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or JADU
  Means a residential unit that satisfies all of the following :
  (a) It is no more than 500 square feet in size.
  (b) It is contained entirely within an existing or proposed single-family structure .
  An enclosed use within the residence , such as an attached garage , is considered
  to be a part of and contained within the single-family structure .
  (c) It includes its own separate sanitation facilities or shares sanitation facilities
  with the existing or proposed single-family structure .
  (d) If the unit does not include its own separate bathroom , then it contains an
  interior entrance to the main living area of the existing or proposed single-family
  structure in addition to an exterior entrance that is separate from the main
  entrance to the primary dwelling .
  (e) It includes an efficiency kitchen , as defined in this subsection above .
LIVABLE SPACE
  Means a space in a dwelling intended for human habitation , including living ,
  sleeping, eating , cooking , or sanitation .
LIVING AREA
  Means the interior habitable area of a dwelling unit, including basements and
  attics, but does not include a garage or any accessory structure.
NONCONFORMING ZONING CONDITION
  Means a physical improvement on a property that does not conform with current
  zoning standards.
PASSAGEWAY
  Means a pathway that is unobstructed clear to the sky and extends from a street
  to one entrance of the ADU or JADU .
PROPOSED DWELLING
   Means a dwelling that is the subject of a permit application and that meets the
  requirements for permitting.
PUBLIC TRANSIT
  Means a location, including, but not limited to , a bus stop or train station , where
  the public may access buses, trains, subways, and other forms of transportation
  that charge set fares, run on fixed routes , and are available to the public. Access
  to the City of Avalon Seaside Transit (COAST) on-demand transit system shall
  also qualify as public transit for the purposes of this article .
TANDEM PARKING
  Means that two or more automobiles are parked on a driveway or in any other
  location on a lot, lined up behind one another.

  must match the appearance and architectural design of those of the primary
  dwelling .

  by the building or fire code.
  (3) The ADU must have an independent exterior entrance , apart from that of the
  primary dwelling.

  every direction , with a minimum interior wall height of seven feet.

  no direct line of sight or screened using fencing , landscaping, or privacy glass to
  prevent a direct line of sight.

  that is not a public right-of-way line must either be (for windows) clerestory with
  the bottom of the glass at least six feet above the finished floor, or (for windows
  and for doors) utilize frosted or obscure glass.

  dwelling . The dominant roof slope is the slope shared by the largest portion of the
  roof.

of the underlying zone.

story, except that an ADU that is attached to the primary dwelling may have the stories
allowed under subsection 9-5.605(b)(4) .

5.604(a) or 9-5.604(b) above.

  charge for water or sewer service.

   covered by subsection 9-5.607(b)(2) require a new, separate utility connection
  directly between the ADU and the utility for any utility that is provided by the city.

  a. The connection is subject to a connection fee or capacity charge that is

§ 9-5.601 Purpose.

§ 9-5.602 Effect of Conforming.

§ 9-5.603 Definitions.
As used in this section , terms are defined as follows :
ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or ADU
  Means an attached or a detached residential dwelling unit that provides complete
  independent living facilities for one or more persons and is located on a lot with a
  proposed or existing primary residence . An accessory dwelling unit also includes
  the following:
   (a) An efficiency unit, as defined by section 17958.1 of the California Health and
  Safety Code ; and
  (b) A manufactured home, as defined by section 18007 of the California Health
  and Safety Code.
ACCESSORY STRUCTURE
  Means a structure that is accessory and incidental to a dwelling located on the
  same lot.
COMPLETE INDEPENDENT LIVING FACILITIES
  Means permanent provisions for living , sleeping , eating , cooking , and sanitation
  on the same parcel as the single-family or multifamily dwelling is or will be
  situated .
EFFICIENCY KITCHEN
  Means a kitchen that includes all of the following:
  (a) A cooking facility with appliances.
  (b) A food preparation counter and storage cabinets that are of a reasonable size
  in relation to the size of the JADU.
JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or JADU
  Means a residential unit that satisfies all of the following :
  (a) It is no more than 500 square feet in size .
  (b) It is contained entirely within an existing or proposed single-family structure.
  An enclosed use within the residence , such as an attached garage , is considered
  to be a part of and contained within the single-family structure .
  (c) It includes its own separate sanitation facilities or shares sanitation facilities
  with the existing or proposed single-family structure.
  (d) If the unit does not include its own separate bathroom , then it contains an
  interior entrance to the main living area of the existing or proposed single-family
  structure in addition to an exterior entrance that is separate from the main
  entrance to the primary dwelling.
  (e) It includes an efficiency kitchen , as defined in this subsection above.
LIVABLE SPACE
  Means a space in a dwelling intended for human habitation, including living,
  sleeping, eating, cooking, or sanitation.
LIVING AREA
  Means the interior habitable area of a dwelling unit, including basements and
  attics , but does not include a garage or any accessory structure.
 NONCONFORMING ZONING CONDITION
  Means a physical improvement on a property that does not conform with current
  zoning standards .
PASSAGEWAY
  Means a pathway that is unobstructed clear to the sky and extends from a street
  to one entrance of the ADU or JADU.
PROPOSED DWELLING
  Means a dwelling that is the subject of a permit application and that meets the
  requirements for permitting .
PUBLIC TRANSIT
  Means a location , including, but not limited to , a bus stop or train station , where
  the public may access buses, trains, subways , and other forms of transportation
  that charge set fares , run on fixed routes , and are available to the public. Access
  to the City of Avalon Seaside Transit (COAST) on-demand transit system shall
  also qualify as public transit for the purposes of this article .
TANDEM PARKING
  Means that two or more automobiles are parked on a driveway or in any other
  location on a lot, lined up behind one another.

§ 9-5.605 General ADU and JADU Requirements.
The following requirements apply to all ADUs and JADUs that are approved under
subsections 9-5.604(a) or 9-5.604(b) above:
(a) Zoning .
  (1) An ADU or JADU subject only to a building permit under subsection 9-604(a)
  above may be created on a lot in a residential or mixed-use zone.
  (2) An ADU or JADU subject to an ADU permit under subsection 9-
  5.604(b) above may be created on a lot that is zoned to allow single-family
  dwelling residential use or multifamily dwelling residential use.
  (3) In accordance with Government Code section 66333(a), a JADU may only be
  created on a lot zoned for single-family residences.
(b) Height.
  (1) Except as otherwise provided by subsections 9-5.605(b)(2) and 9-
  5.605(b)(3) below, a detached ADU created on a lot with an existing or proposed
   single family or multifamily dwelling unit may not exceed 16 feet in height.
  (2) A detached ADU may be up to 18 feet in height if it is created on a lot with an
  existing or proposed single family or multifamily dwelling unit that is located within
  one-half mile walking distance of a major transit stop or a high quality transit
  corridor, as those terms are defined in Section 21155 of the Public Resources
  Code, and the ADU may be up to two additional feet in height (for a maximum of
  20 feet) if necessary to accommodate a roof pitch on the ADU that is aligned with
  the roof pitch of the primary dwelling unit.
  (3) A detached ADU created on a lot with an existing or proposed multifamily
  dwelling that has more than one story above grade may not exceed 18 feet in
  height.
  (4) An ADU that is attached to the primary dwelling may not exceed 25 feet in
  height or the height limitation imposed by the underlying zone that applies to the
  primary dwelling , whichever is lower. Notwithstanding the foregoing , ADUs
  subject to this subsection 9-5.605(b)(4) may not exceed two stories .
  (5) For purposes of this subsection 9-5.605(b) , height is measured above from
  existing legal grade or the level of the lowest floor, whichever is lower, to the peak
  of the structure .
(c) Fire Sprinklers.
  (1) Fire sprinklers are required in an ADU if sprinklers are required in the primary
  residence .
  (2) The construction of an ADU does not trigger a requirement for fire sprinklers
  to be installed in the existing primary dwelling .
(d) Rental Term. No ADU or JADU may be rented for a term that is shorter than 30 days.
This prohibition applies regardless of when the ADU or JADU was created .
(e) No Separate Conveyance. An ADU or JADU may be rented , but, except as otherwise
provided in Government Code Section 66341 65852.26 , no ADU or JADU may be sold
or otherwise conveyed separately from the lot and the primary dwelling (in the case of a
single-family lot) or from the lot and all of the dwellings (in the case of a multifamily lot).
(f) Septic System. If the ADU or JADU will connect to an onsite wastewater-treatment
system , the owner must include with the application a percolation test completed within
the last five years or, if the percolation test has been recertified , within the last 10 years.
(g) Owner Occupancy.
  (1) AA-ADUs created under this section on or after January 1, 2020 that is
  permitted after January 1, 2020 , but before January 1, 2025 , +s are not subject to
  any owner-occupancy requirement.
  (2) Unless applicable law requires otherwise , all ADUs that are permitted on or
  after January 1, 2025 are subject to an mvner occupancy requirement. A natural
  person with legal or equitable title to the property must reside on the property as
   the person's legal domicile and permanent residence .
  {3}--(2) As required by state law, all JADUs are subject to an owner-occupancy
  requirement. A natural person with legal or equitable title to the property must
  reside on the property, in either the primary dwelling or JADU , as the person's
  legal domicile and permanent residence . However, the owner-occupancy
  requirement in this subsection 9-5.605(g)(3) does not apply if the property is
  entirely owned by another governmental agency, land trust, or housing
  organization.
(h) Deed Restriction . Prior to issuance of a building permit for an ADU or JADU , a deed
restriction must be recorded against the title of the property in the County Recorder's
office and a copy filed with the Director (or their designee) and filed with the Planning
Department. The deed restriction must run with the land and bind all future owners . The
form of the deed restriction will be provided by the City and must provide that:
  (1) Except as otherwise provided in Government Code Section 66341 65852 .26,
  the ADU or JADU may not be sold separately from the primary dwelling.
  (2) The ADU or JADU is restricted to the approved size and to other attributes
  allowed by this section .
  (3) The deed restriction runs with the land and may be enforced against future
  property owners .
  (4) The deed restriction may be removed if the owner eliminates the ADU or
  JADU , as evidenced by, for example , removal of the kitchen facilities . To remove
  the deed restriction , an owner may make a written request of the Director,

  ADU or JADU has been eliminated. Appeal may be taken from the Director's

  is not entirely physically removed , but is only eliminated by virtue of having a
  necessary component of an ADU or JADU removed , the remaining structure and

  (5) The deed restriction is enforceable by the Director or his or her designee for

  JADU during the prior year. If the City does not receive the report within the 90-

  (1) Must comply with building code . Subject to subsection 9-5.6050)(2) below, all

  DISCUSSION AND RECOMMENDATIONS

Program #14 - Accessory Dwelling Units:

Accessory dwelling units (A DUs) and junior accessory dwelling units (JADUs) help meet the
City ' s housing needs for all income levels and also provide a housing resource for seniors and
low- and moderate-income households throughout the entire community . In accordance with
State law, accessory units (also known as second units or granny flats) are allowed by right in
 all residential zones within the city. Chapter 9-5, Artic le 6, Accessory Dwelling Units,
provides specific development standards and processing requirements for ADUs.

Program #14 requires that the City continue to amend the ordinance based on future changes
to State law and work with the California Department of Housing and Community
Development (HCD) to ensure continued compliance with State law. The City will also
continue to monitor the extent of ADU production to ensure that the ordinance modifications
are successful and that the Housing Element goals can be met.

SB 1211 and AB 2553, adopted in 2024 and effective as of January 1, 2025 , are the most
recent legislative acts that include multiple updates to State ADU law which clarify the
development requirements for ADUs. Below is a summary of the amendments proposed to
comply with current State law requirements:

  •  Update Government Code and Health and Safety Code legal references throughout.
  •  Add definition for " livable space". (Section 9-5.603)
  •  Clarify the number of detached ADUs permitted on a lot with proposed multi-family
  development. (Section 9-5.604.a.4)
  •  Clarify that JADUs are only permitted on lots zoned for single-family residences.
  (Section 9-5.605.a.3)
  •  Clarify the method of measuring the height of an ADU. (Section 9-5.605.b.5)
  •  Remove owner-occupancy requirement for ADUs constructed after January I, 2025.
  (Section 9-5.605.g. I and 2)
  •  Clarify that unco vered parking spaces are included in the types of off-street parking
  that do not need to be replaced when an ADU is constructed (Section 9-5.606.g.3)
  •  Add clarification of the number of allowed stories for an ADU. (Section 9-6.606.j)

In addition, Staff has reviewed the objective architectural design standards for ADUs to
identify opportunities to clarify requirements and reduce impediments for ADU development.
The following amendments are proposed to update the design standards for ADUs:

  •  Clarify the architectural requirements for window and door placement and privacy
  screening. (Section 9-5.606.h.5)
  •  Add architectural requirement that roof slope must match that of the dominant roof
  slope of the primary dwelling on a lot. (Section 9-5.606.h.7)
  •  Revise the requirements for site landscaping to require compliance with the objective
  standards of the underlying zone. (Section 9-5.606.i)

 The proposed ordinance is exempt from the provisions of the California Environmental Quality

The General Plan is a long-term policy guide for the development of the City but does not propose

addendum to the Program EIR was prepared which concluded that the Housing Element updates
do not result in any new or greater environmental impacts than were previously analyzed,
disclosed, and mitigated .

Pursuant to Public Resources Code section 21083.3 and CEQA Guideline 15 I 83(a) , a project that
is consistent with the development densities establi shed in a General Plan for which an EIR was
certified is not required to undergo additional environmental review "except as might be necessary
to examine whether there are project-specific significant effects which are peculiar to the project
or its site." As noted above, an EIR was certified for the General Plan. The proposed amendments
contained in the ordinance do not authorize construction and make minor changes to ex isting
standards and land use limitations that apply to existing uses permitted in residential zones in the
City and allow uses that are consistent with the residential uses currently permitted in such zones.

In addition, Guideline 15061 (b )(3) states that a project is exempt from CEQA if the activity
covered by the common sense exemption that CEQA only applies to projects which have the
potential for causing a significant effect on the e nvironment. The proposed amendments provide
standards for the approval of allowed growth within the parameters of existing General Plan and
municipal code regulations. It does not authorize any changes to land use limitations or approve
any new development project. Therefore, there is no reasonable possibility that the activity in
question may have a significant effect on the environment.

Environmental Quality Act (" CEQA") does not apply to the adoption of an ordinance by a city or

 county implementing the provisions of Section 65852.1 or Section 65852.2 of the Government

66313. Therefore, the component of the ordinance which implements state ADU law is statutorily
exempt from CEQA.

Therefore, it can be seen with certainty that the draft ordinance has no potential to cause a
significant effect on the environment, and the amendments themselves are categorically exempt
from further review under CEQA pursuant to Sections l 5 l 83(a) and 15061 (b)(3) of the California
Code of Regulations.

§ 9-5.60 I Purpose.
The purpose of this section is to allow and regulate accessory dwelling units (AD Us) and junior
accessory dwelling units (JADUs) in compliance with Chapter 13 of Division I of Title 7 of the
California Government Code.

§ 9-5.602 Effect of Conforming.
An ADU or JADU that conforms to the standards in this section will not be:
(a) Deemed to be inconsistent with the City's general plan and zoning designation for the lot on
which the ADU or JADU is located.
(b) Deemed to exceed the allowable density for the lot on which the ADU or JADU is located.
(c) Considered in the application of any local ordinance, policy, or program to limit residential
growth.
(d) Required to correct a nonconforming zoning condition, as defined in subsection 9-
5.603 below. This does not prevent the City from enforcing compliance with appl icable building
standards in accordance with Health and Safety Code section 17980.12.

§ 9-5.603 Definitions.
As used in this section , terms are defined as follows:
ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or ADU
  Means an attached or a detached residential dwelling unit that provides complete
  independent living facilities for one or more persons and is located on a lot with a
  proposed or existing primary residence. An accessory dwelling unit also includes the
  following:
  (a) An efficiency unit, as defined by section 17958.1 of the California Health and Safety
  Code; and
  (b) A manufactured home, as defined by section 18007 of the California Health and
  Safety Code.
ACCESSORY STRUCTURE
  Means a structure that is accessory and incidental to a dwelling located on the same lot.
COMPLETE INDEPENDENT LIVING FACILITIES
  Means permanent provisions for living, sleeping, eating, cooking, and sanitation on the
   same parcel as the single-family or multifamily dwelling is or will be situated.
EFFICIENCY KITCHEN
  Means a kitchen that includes all of the following:
  (a) A cooking facility with appliances.
  (b) A food preparation counter and storage cabinets that are of a reasonable size in relation
  to the size of the JADU.
JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or JADU
  Means a residential unit that satisfies all of the fo llowing :
  (a) It is no more than 500 square feet in size.
  (b) It is contained entirely within an existing or proposed si ngle-family structure. An
  enclosed use within the residence, such as an attached garage, is cons idered to be a part
  of and contained within the single-family structure .
  (c) It includes its own separate sanitation facilities or shares sanitation facilities with the
  existing or proposed single-family structure.
  (d) If the unit does not include its own separate bathroom , then it contains an interior
  entrance to the main living area of the existing or proposed single-family structure in
  addition to an exterior entrance that is separate from the main entrance to the primary
  dwelling.
  (e) It includes an efficiency kitchen , as defined in this subsection above.
LIVABLE SP ACE
  Means a space in a dwelling intended for human habitation, including living, sleeping,
  eating, cooking, or sanitation .
LIVING AREA
  Means the interior habitable area of a dwelling unit, including basements and attics, but
  does not include a garage or any accessory structure.
NONCONFORMING ZONING CONDITION
  Means a physical improvement on a property that does not conform with current zoning
  standards .
PASSAGEWAY
  Means a pathway that is unobstructed clear to the sky and extends from a street to one
  entrance of the ADU or JADU .
PROPOSED DWELLING
  Means a dwelling that is the subject of a permit application and that meets the
  requirements for permitting.
 PUBLIC TRANSIT
  Means a location, including, but not limited to, a bus stop or train station, where the public
  may access buses, trains, subways, and other forms of transportation that charge set fares ,
  run on fixed routes, and are available to the public.
TANDEM PARKING
  Means that two or more automobiles are parked on a driveway or in any other location on
  a lot, lined up behind one another.

in subsection 9-5.605 below, it is allowed with only a building permit in the following scenarios:

  5.604(a)(I) and one JADU on a lot with a proposed or existing single-fami ly dwelling on
  it, where the ADU or JADU:

  existing space of an exist ing single-fam il y dwelling; or (in the case of an ADU
  only) within the existing space of an accessory structure, plus up to 150 additional
  square feet if the expansion is limited to accommodating ingress and egress; and
  b. Has exterior access that is independent of that for the single-family dwelling;
  and
  c. Has side and rear setbacks sufficient for fire and safety, as dictated by applicable

  d. The JADU complies with the requirements of Government Code sections
  66333 through 66339.
  (2) Limited Detached on Single-fam il y Lot: One detached, new-construction ADU on a

  b. The total floor area is 800 square feet or smaller.

   subsection 9-5.604(a)(3), at least one converted ADU is allowed within an ex1stmg

  limitations:
  a. The side- and rear-yard setbacks are at least three feet. If the existing
  multifamily dwelling has a rear or side yard setback of less than four feet, the City

  b. The peak height above grade does not exceed the applicable height limit

  c. If the lot has an existing multifamily dwelling, the quantity of detached AD Us

  b. When an application to create an ADU or JADU is submitted with a permit

§ 9-5.605 General ADU and JADU Requirements.
The following requirements apply to all AD Us and JADUs that are approved under subsections 9-
5.604(a) or 9-5.604(b) above:
(a) Zoning.
  (1) An ADU or JADU subject only to a building permit under subsection 9-604(a) above
  may be created on a lot in a residential or mixed-use zone.
  (2) An ADU or JADU subject to an ADU permit under subsection 9-5.604(b) above may
  be created on a lot that is zoned to allow single-family dwelling residential use or
  multifamily dwelling residential use .
  (3) In accordance with Government Code section 66333(a), a JADU may only be created
  on a lot zoned for single-family residences.
(b) Height.
  (1) Except as otherwise provided by subsections 9-5.605(b)(2) and 9-5 .605(b)(3) below,
  a detached ADU created on a lot with an existing or proposed single family or multifamily
  dwelling unit may not exceed 16 feet in height.
  (2) A detached ADU may be up to 18 feet in height if it is created on a lot with an existing
  or proposed single family or multifamil y dwelling unit that is located within one-half mile
  walking distance of a major transit sto p or a high quality transit corridor, as those terms
  are defined in Section 21155 of the Public Resources Code, and the ADU may be up to
  two additional feet in height (for a maximum of 20 feet) if necessary to accommodate a
  roof pitch on the ADU that is aligned with the roof pitch of the primary dwelling unit.
  (3) A detached ADU created on a lot with an existing or proposed multifamily dwelling
  that has more than one story above grade may not exceed 18 feet in height.
  (4) An ADU that is attached to the primary dwelling may not exceed 25 feet in height or
  the height limitation imposed by the underl y ing zone that applies to the primary dwelling,
  whichever is lower. Notwithstanding the foregoing , ADUs subject to this subsection 9-
  5.605(b)(4) may not exceed two stories.
  (5) For purposes of this subsection 9-5.605(b), height is measured from existing legal
  grade or the level of the lowest floor, whichever is lower, to the peak of the structure.
(c) Fire Sprinklers.
   (1) Fire sprinklers are required in an ADU if sprinklers are required in the primary
  residence .
  (2) The construction of an ADU does not trigger a requirement for fire sprinklers to be
  installed in the existing primary dwelling.
(d) Rental Term. No ADU or JADU may be rented for a term that is shorter than 30 days. This
prohibition applies regardless of when the ADU or JADU was created .
(e) No Separate Conveyance. An ADU or JADU may be rented, but, except as otherwise provided
in Government Code Section 6634 I, no ADU or JADU may be sold or otherwise conveyed
separately from the lot and the primary dwelling (in the case of a single-family lot) or from the
lot and all of the dwellings (in the case of a multifamily lot).
(f) Septic System. If the ADU or JADU will connect to an onsite wastewater-treatment system ,
the owner must include with the application a percolation test completed within the last five years
or, if the percolation test has been recertified , within the last IO years.
(g) Owner Occupancy.
  (1) ADUs created under this section on or after January I, 2020 are not subject to any
  owner-occupancy requirement.
  (2) As required by state law, all JADUs are subject to an owner-occupancy requirement.
  A natural person with legal or equitable title to the property must reside on the property,
  in either the primary dwelling or JADU , as the person's legal domicile and permanent
  residence. However, the owner-occupancy requirement in this subsection 9-
  5.605(g)(3) does not apply if the property is entirely owned by another governmental
  agency, land trust, or housing organization.
(h) Deed Restriction . Prior to issuance of a building permit for an ADU or JADU , a deed
restriction must be recorded against the title of the property in the County Recorder's office and
a copy filed with the Director (or their designee) and filed with the Planning Department. The
deed restriction must run with the land and bind all future owners. The form of the deed restriction
will be provided by the City and must provide that:
  (1) Except as otherwise provided in Government Code Section 66341 , the ADU or JADU
  may not be sold separately from the primary dwelling.
  (2) The ADU or JADU is restricted to the approved size and to other attributes allowed
  by this section.
  (3) The deed restriction runs with the land and may be enforced against future property
  owners.
  (4) The deed restriction may be removed if the owner eliminates the ADU or JADU , as
  evidenced by, for example, removal of the kitchen facilities. To remove the deed
  restriction, an owner may make a written request of the Director, providing evidence that
  the ADU or JADU has in fact been eliminated. The Director may then determine whether
  the evidence supports the claim that the ADU or JADU has been eliminated. Appeal may
  be taken from the Director's determination consistent with other provisions of this Code.
  If the ADU or JADU is not entirely physically removed, but is only eliminated by virtue
   of having a necessary component of an ADU or JADU removed, the remaining structure
  and improvements must otherwise comply with applicable provisions of this Code.
  (5) The deed restriction is enforceable by the Director or his or her designee for the benefit
  of the City. Failure of the property owner to comply with the deed restriction may result
  in legal action against the property owner, and the City is authorized to obtain any remedy
  available to it at law or equity, including, but not limited to, obtaining an injunction
  enjoining the use of the ADU or JADU in violation of the recorded restrictions or
  abatement of the ilie gal unit.
(i) Income Reporting. In order to facilitate the City's obligation to identify adequate sites for
housing in accordance with Government Code sections 65583 . 1 and 66330 , the following
requirements must be satisfied:
  (1) With the building-permit application, the applicant must provide the City with an
  estimate of the projected annualized rent that will be charged for the ADU or JADU.
  (2) Within 90 days after each January l_of the issuance of the building permit, the owner
  must report the actual rent charged for the ADU or JADU during the prior year. If the
  City does not receive the report within the 90-day period, the owner is in violation of this
  Code, and the City may send the owner a notice of violation and allow the owner another

  (1) Must comply with building code. Subject to subsection 9-5 .605(j)(2) below, all AD Us

The following requirements apply only to ADUs that require an ADU permit under subsection 9-
5.604(b) above.

  (1) The maximum size of a detached or attached ADU subject to this subsection 9-5 .606 is
  850 square feet for a studio or one-bedroom unit and 1,000 square feet for a unit with two

  b. The ADU is located within an architecturally and historically significant

  d. When on-street parking permits are required but not offered to the occupant of

  e. When there is an established car share vehicle stop located within one block of

§ 9-5.601 Purpose.
The purpose of this section is to allow and regulate accessory dwelling units (AD Us) and
junior accessory dwelling units (JADUs) in compliance with California Government
Code sections 65852 .2 and 65852.22 . Chapter 13 of Division 1 of Title 7 of the California
Government Code.

§ 9-5.602 Effect of Conforming.
An ADU or JADU that conforms to the standards in this section will not be :
(a) Deemed to be inconsistent with the City's general plan and zoning designation for
the lot on which the ADU or JADU is located .
(b) Deemed to exceed the allowable density for the lot on which the ADU or JADU is
located.
(c) Considered in the application of any local ordinance , policy, or program to limit
residential growth .
(d) Required to correct a nonconforming zoning condition, as defined in subsection 9-
5.603 below. This does not prevent the City from enforcing compliance with applicable
building standards in accordance with Health and Safety Code section 17980.12.

§ 9-5.603 Definitions.
As used in this section , terms are defined as follows:
ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or ADU
  Means an attached or a detached residential dwelling unit that provides complete
  independent living facilities for one or more persons and is located on a lot with a
  proposed or existing primary residence . An accessory dwelling unit also includes
  the following:
   (a) An efficiency unit, as defined by section 17958.1 of the California Health and
  Safety Code; and
  (b) A manufactured home , as defined by section 18007 of the California Health
  and Safety Code .
ACCESSORY STRUCTURE
  Means a structure that is accessory and incidental to a dwelling located on the
  same lot.
COMPLETE INDEPENDENT LIVING FACILITIES
  Means permanent provisions for living , sleeping , eating , cooking , and sanitation
  on the same parcel as the single-family or multifamily dwelling is or will be
  situated .
EFFICIENCY KITCHEN
  Means a kitchen that includes all of the following :
  (a) A cooking facility with appliances .
  (b) A food preparation counter and storage cabinets that are of a reasonable size
  in relation to the size of the JADU.
JUNIOR ACCESSORY DWELLING UNIT or JADU
  Means a residential unit that satisfies all of the following :
  (a) It is no more than 500 square feet in size .
  (b) It is contained entirely within an existing or proposed single-family structure.
  An enclosed use within the residence , such as an attached garage , is considered
  to be a part of and contained within the single-family structure .
  (c) It includes its own separate sanitation facilities or shares sanitation facilities
  with the existing or proposed single-family structure.
  (d) If the unit does not include its own separate bathroom , then it contains an
  interior entrance to the main living area of the existing or proposed single-family
  structure in addition to an exterior entrance that is separate from the main
  entrance to the primary dwelling.
  (e) It includes an efficiency kitchen , as defined in this subsection above.
LIVABLE SPACE
  Means a space in a dwelling intended for human habitation, including living,
  sleeping, eating , cooking, or sanitation .
LIVING AREA
  Means the interior habitable area of a dwelling unit, including basements and
  attics , but does not include a garage or any accessory structure.
 NONCONFORMING ZONING CONDITION
  Means a physical improvement on a property that does not conform with current
  zoning standards.
PASSAGEWAY
  Means a pathway that is unobstructed clear to the sky and extends from a street
  to one entrance of the ADU or JADU.
PROPOSED DWELLING
  Means a dwelling that is the subject of a permit application and that meets the
  requirements for permitting .
PUBLIC TRANSIT
  Means a location , including , but not limited to , a bus stop or train station , where
  the public may access buses , trains , subways, and other forms of transportation
  that charge set fares , run on fixed routes , and are available to the public.
TANDEM PARKING
  Means that two or more automobiles are parked on a driveway or in any other
  location on a lot, lined up behind one another.

§ 9-5.604 Approvals.

(a) Building-permit Only. If an ADU or JADU complies with each of the general
requirements in subsection 9-5.605 below, it is allowed with only a building permit in the
following scenarios:
  (1) Converted on Single-family Lot: One ADU as described in this subsection 9-
  5.604(a)(1) and one JADU on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family
  dwelling on it, where the ADU or JADU :
  a. Is either: within the space of a proposed single-family dwelling ; within
  the existing space of an existing single-family dwelling ; or (in the case of
  an ADU only) within the existing space of an accessory structure, plus up
  to 150 additional square feet if the expansion is limited to accommodating
  ingress and egress; and
  b. Has exterior access that is independent of that for the single-family
  dwelling; and
  c. Has side and rear setbacks sufficient for fire and safety, as dictated by
  applicable building and fire codes.
  d. The JADU complies with the requirements  of Government
  Code Section 65852 .22 . sections 66333 through 66339.
   (2) Limited Detached on Single-family Lot: One detached , new-construction ADU
  on a lot with a proposed or existing single-family dwelling (in addition to any JADU
  that might otherwise be established on the lot under subsection 9-
  5.604(a)(1) above) , if the detached ADU satisfies each of the following limitations:
  a. The side- and rear-yard setbacks are at least three feet.
  b. The total floor area is 800 square feet or smaller.

§ 9-5.605 General ADU and JADU Requirements.
The following requirements apply to all ADUs and JADUs that are approved under
subsections 9-5.604(a) or 9-5.604(b) above:
(a) Zoning .
  (1) An ADU or JADU subject only to a building permit under subsection 9-604(a)
  above may be created on a lot in a residential or mixed-use zone.
  (2) An ADU or JADU subject to an ADU permit under subsection 9-
  5.604(b) above may be created on a lot that is zoned to allow single-family
  dwelling residential use or multifamily dwelling residential use.
  (3) In accordance with Government Code section 66333(a), a JADU may only be
  created on a lot zoned for single-family residences .
(b) Height.
  (1) Except as otherwise provided by subsections 9-5 .605(b)(2) and 9-
  5.605(b)(3) below, a detached ADU created on a lot with an existing or proposed
  single family or multifamily dwelling unit may not exceed 16 feet in height.
  (2) A detached ADU may be up to 18 feet in height if it is created on a lot with an
   existing or proposed single family or multifamily dwelling unit that is located within
  one-half mile walking distance of a major transit stop or a high quality transit
  corridor, as those terms are defined in Section 21155 of the Public Resources
  Code, and the ADU may be up to two additional feet in height (for a maximum of
  20 feet) if necessary to accommodate a roof pitch on the ADU that is aligned with
  the roof pitch of the primary dwelling unit.
  (3) A detached ADU created on a lot with an existing or proposed multifamily
  dwelling that has more than one story above grade may not exceed 18 feet in
  height.
  (4) An ADU that is attached to the primary dwelling may not exceed 25 feet in
  height or the height limitation imposed by the underlying zone that applies to the
  primary dwelling , whichever is lower. Notwithstanding the foregoing, ADUs
  subject to this subsection 9-5 .605(b)(4) may not exceed two stories.

  existing legal grade or the level of the lowest floor, whichever is lower, to the peak

  residence.

§ 9-5 .606 Specific ADU Requirements.
The following requirements apply only to ADUs that require an ADU permit under
subsection 9-5.604(b) above.
(a) Maximum Size .
  (1) The maximum size of a detached or attached ADU subject to this
  subsection 9-5.606 is 850 square feet for a studio or one-bedroom unit and 1,000
  square feet for a unit with two or more bedrooms .
  (2) An attached ADU that is created on a lot with an existing primary dwelling is
  further limited to 50% of the floor area of the existing primary dwelling .
  (3) Application of other development standards in this subsection 9-5.606, such
  as FAR or lot coverage, might further limit the size of the ADU , but no application
  of the percent-based size limit in subsection 9-5 .606(a)(2) above or of an FAR ,
  front setback, lot coverage limit, or open-space requirement may require the ADU
  to be less than 800 square feet.
(b) Floor Area Ratio (FAR). No ADU subject to this subsection 9-5.606 may cause the
total FAR of the lot to exceed 45% , subject to subsection 9-5 .606(a)(3) above .
(c) Setbacks .
  (1) An ADU that is subject to this subsection 9-5.606 must conform to a 3-foot
  front-yard setback, subject to subsection 9-5 .606(a)(3) above.
  (2) An ADU that is subject to this subsection 9-5.606 must conform to 3-foot side-
   and rear-yard setbacks.
  (3) No setback is required for an ADU that is subject to this subsection 9-5.606 if
  the ADU is constructed in the same location and to the same dimensions as an
  existing structure .
(d) Lot Coverage . No ADU subject to this subsection 9-5.606 may cause the total lot
coverage of the lot to exceed 50% , subject to subsection 9-5.606(a)(3) above.
(e) Minimum Open Space . No ADU subject to this subsection 9-5 .606 may cause the
total percentage of open space of the lot to fall below 50% , subject to subsection 9-
5.606(a)(3) above .
(f) Passageway. No passageway, as defined by subsection 9-5.603 above , is required
for an ADU .
(g) Parking .
  (1) Generally. One off-street parking space is required for each ADU . The parking
  space may be provided in setback areas or as tandem parking , as defined by
  subsection 9-5.603 above .
  (2) Exceptions. No parking under subsection 9-5 .606(g)(1) is required in the
  following situations:
  a. The ADU is located within one-half mile walking distance of public
  transit, as defined in subsection 9-5.603 above.
  b. The ADU is located within an architecturally and historically significant
  historic district.
  c. The ADU is part of the proposed or existing primary residence or an
  accessory structure under subsection 9-5.604(a)(1) above.
  d. When on-street parking permits are required but not offered to the
  occupant of the ADU.

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S) : Per the City's procurement policy, authorize the City Manager
or designee , to execute an agreement with Perry Plumbing & Pipelining to provide maintenance
services for the installation of epoxy lining of two verified clay sewer mains in the amount not to
exceed $32 ,036 .

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon maintains an extensive sewer collection system ,
portions of which are constructed of verified clay pipe (VCP) . Over time, these lines are prone
to cracking and root intrusion , which cause blockages, backups , and costly emergency repairs.
To extend the service life of existing public works infrastructure, staff have identified two
segments of sewer main requiring epoxy lining rehabilitation :
  1. Burma Trail Sewer Main : 4-inch diameter VCP , approximately 132 feet in length .
  2. Joe Machado Field Sewer Main : 10-inch diameter VCP , approximately 10 feet in length .
Epoxy lining is a trenchless rehabilitation method that coats the interior of an existing sewer main
with a corrosion-resistant epoxy. This method eliminates infiltration , prevents root intrusion , and
restores structural integrity without the need for costly excavation . The selected product includes
a twenty-year warranty against root intrusion and a fifty-year manufacturer guarantee. Staff
solicited quotes from multiple plumbing contractors to perform the lining work:
